reconstructed_theorem_text: For every measurable space X, every extended nonnegative measure mu on X, and every pair of functions a,b:X to [0,infinity], assume a and b are measurable up to a mu-null set, 0<b(x)<infinity for mu-almost every x, and 0<integral b dmu<infinity. Then for every real q>1, (integral a dmu)^q/(integral b dmu)^(q-1) is at most integral a(x)^q/b(x)^(q-1) dmu(x). Every displayed integral is the extended nonnegative Lebesgue integral, and powers and division use extended nonnegative real conventions. No finiteness assumption is imposed on a, its integral, or the right-hand integral; in particular integral a=infinity is included. No probability, finite-total-mass, or sigma-finiteness hypothesis is imposed on mu. There are no additional constants. No ambiguity in the quantified inequality using the supplied extended-real conventions.
